sources.fullCitation: Jan Kiepura with the Odeon-Künstler-Orchester conducted by Dr. Weissmann. “Oh Madonna!”, from Ein Lied für dich; label credits music to B. Kaper and Walter Jurmann and words to Fritz Rotter and Ernst Marischka. Odeon O-4707 a, matrix Be 10220, take 2; recorded 11 February 1933. Disc label photograph and audio transfer published by the Great 78 Project, Internet Archive.
sources.title: Oh Madonna! — Odeon O-4707 a
sources.creator: Jan Kiepura; Odeon Künstler-Orchester
sources.researchNote: The photograph identifies Odeon O-4707 a, matrix Be 10220, and the runout shows take 2. Christian Zwarg’s Odeon matrix discography lists Be 10220-2 under 11 February 1933, Berlin, Schlesische Straße 26, room 2, with Jan Kiepura and Frieder Weissmann. The indexed PDF text was consulted; the complete file could not be retrieved during this review. Internet Archive instead supplies 1932 without a stated basis; that year conflicts with the matrix chronology and is not adopted. The structured date describes the recording session, not the issue or manufacture of this copy. Henry König’s Odeon label list separately lists O-4707 under 1933 but leaves the release-date column empty. The label does not identify Wiener Boheme-Verlag as the sheet-music publisher.

sources.creator: Hans Albers, with the Odeon-Künstler-Orchester under Otto Dobrindt
sources.researchNote: Henry König’s Odeon label list identifies Hans Albers, Odeon O-11811, matrix Be 10227-2, a session in Berlin, room 2, on 13 February 1933, and release in April 1933. Christian Zwarg’s Odeon matrix discography separately names Otto Dobrindt as musical director with orchestra and Hans Albers for Be 10227 and Be 10227-2; it does not name the orchestra. The upload description gives Be 10227 without a take suffix, identifies the Odeon-Künstler-Orchester and names Dobrindt. sources.title: Signorina, signorina — Odeon O.236842 b
sources.creator: Jan Kiepura; Odeon symphony orchestra
sources.researchNote: The label is clearly visible: O.236842 b, number 137013, Jan Kiepura, the Odeon symphony orchestra and “Śpiew polski”. It prints the three credited names and the Polish film title. The number 137013 is transcribed as printed, without assigning an unverified matrix prefix or take. SRC0633 independently catalogues the coupled disc O.236842 and supplies only [post 1930], not an exact session or issue date; the issue of the photographed copy remains undated here. The upload was published on 12 September 2023. The earlier caption’s claim that the recording could not be identified from discographic detail was incorrect. The label lists the three names without assigning their roles; the composer/lyricist allocation follows the Biblioteka Narodowa catalogue in SRC0633, not the order of names alone.

sources.shortCitation: YouTube, Dajos Béla, “Du liebst mich nicht mehr”
sources.fullCitation: “Du liebst mich nicht mehr.” Slow-fox. YouTube transfer published by Radiomuseum Hardthausen; the uploader identifies Tanz-Orchester Dajos Béla, reports a Berlin recording in 1932 and gives the music credit “Bob Henders”.
sources.title: Du liebst mich nicht mehr — Dajos Béla, YouTube
sources.creator: Tanz-Orchester Dajos Béla
sources.researchNote: The upload reports a music credit to Bob Henders, a Berlin recording in 1932 and an Odeon first issue, but supplies no catalogue or matrix number. It shows a portrait from a Funk-Almanach rather than the label. Henry König’s Odeon label list assigns Be 9946 to this title and also to the coupled “Heute Nacht oder nie!”. The indexed text of Christian Zwarg’s Odeon matrix discography instead lists Be 9946 for “Heute Nacht oder nie!” and Be 9947 for “Du liebst mich nicht mehr”, the latter on Odeon O-11667 b; it dates both sessions to 10 June 1932 in Berlin. The sources therefore differ on this title’s matrix number; the photographed runout or an independent primary witness has not been examined. Neither the disc number nor the exact session date is assigned to the upload without a verified match. The structured year remains the uploader-reported recording year, not a confirmed issue date. The name Bob Henders in these recording descriptions does not by itself resolve the work’s authorship.

works.title: Oh Madonna!
works.publicNote: One tune with two German texts by Ernst Marischka and Fritz Rotter. The song was published, and Hofmeister registered it in May 1933, as “Signorina! komm zu mir”, a 6/8 march-foxtrot; in the film, and on Jan Kiepura’s Odeon disc, it is sung as “Oh Madonna!”. A disc by Carl Jörken is titled “O signorina (O Madonna)” and sings the Madonna text, and the Polish version, “Signorina, signorina”, follows the printed title. The film’s programme prints the song as “Signorina! Serenade” with the words “O Madonna, o Madonna, komm zu mir”. The two were catalogued as separate works until November 2026.

works.title: Mein Gorilla hat ’ne Villa im Zoo
works.sortTitle: Mein Gorilla hat ’ne Villa im Zoo
works.publicNote: The lyric is signed “P. Kuckuck”. Behind the name stood Fritz Rotter, who is credited with the film’s lyrics and who wrote its two other songs under his own name, on prints where Kaper and Jurmann appeared as “Ernst Martin”; the publisher’s house history states that Rotter signed this one number under the pseudonym, in the year all three had to leave Germany. GEMA and the Library of Congress still register Peter Kuckuck as a name of its own.

works.title: Ninon, ach uśmiechnij się!
works.publicNote: Polish-language version, documented by the Odeon disc O. 236842 sung by Jan Kiepura, which names the film by its Polish release title, Zdobyć cię muszę. The disc is undated beyond the catalogue’s [post 1930]; the year given here follows the film. Sieghardt’s opus list (op. 088/PL) gives a Polish version, “Malenka Ninon [Ninon, ach uśmiechnij]”, with words by Jan Wycislik. Jan Wyciślik is a present-day tenor who recorded the song on an undated cassette from Katowice; no other source knows a Polish text by him, and the first line Sieghardt quotes is that of Marcella Halicz’s text.
